hints.title: Offline Query Sorting by Size
hints.text: Sort queries and rooms in descending order of room size to incrementally activate rooms that meet minimum size constraints.

hints.title: Sorted Active ID Collection
hints.text: Store active room IDs in an ordered container to quickly find IDs nearest to the preferred room.

hints.title: Query Closest ID with Tie Breaking
hints.text: Use binary search in the ordered container to evaluate immediate floor and ceiling neighbors to preferred.

hints.title: Full Implementation
hints.text:
```python
import bisect

class Solution:
    def closestRoom(self, rooms: list[list[int]], queries: list[list[int]]) -> list[int]:
        rooms.sort(key=lambda x: -x[1])
        indexed_queries = sorted([(q[1], q[0], i) for i, q in enumerate(queries)], reverse=True)

        active = []
        ans = [-1] * len(queries)
        room_idx = 0
        n = len(rooms)

        for min_sz, pref, q_idx in indexed_queries:
            while room_idx < n and rooms[room_idx][1] >= min_sz:
                bisect.insort(active, rooms[room_idx][0])
                room_idx += 1

            if not active:
                continue

            idx = bisect.bisect_left(active, pref)
            best_id = -1
            min_dist = float('inf')

            if idx < len(active):
                min_dist = active[idx] - pref
                best_id = active[idx]

            if idx > 0:
                dist_left = pref - active[idx - 1]
                if dist_left <= min_dist:
                    best_id = active[idx - 1]

            ans[q_idx] = best_id

        return ans
```

complexity.time: O((n + q) log n + q log q)
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning all rooms for each query takes O(n * q) operations, timing out for 10^5 elements.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Offline descending size sorting with ordered set lookups resolves all queries in O((n + q) log n) time.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate sorts queries offline and queries nearest active ID with binary search.
